title: Indian Community Economic Enhancement Act of 2020
official_summary:
Indian Community Economic Enhancement Act of 2020

This bill makes several revisions related to economic development for Native American communities.

(Sec. 3) Specifically, the bill establishes duties for the Office of Native American Business Development, including (1) advising the Department of Commerce regarding the relationship between the United States and Indian tribes; and (2) serving as the point of contact for tribes, tribal organizations, and members of tribes regarding economic development and doing business in Indian lands.

The bill also requires coordination between Commerce, the Department of the Interior, and the Department of the Treasury to support economic development in Native American communities.

Under the bill, assistance from the Community Development Financial Institutions Fund benefiting Native American institutions does not require matching funds.

The Government Accountability Office must conduct a study that assesses (1) current programs and services that assist Native American communities with business and economic development; (2) assistance provided to Native Americans pursuant to loan, bond, and tax incentive programs; and (3) alternative incentives for tribal governments to invest in a Native American community development investment fund or bank.

(Sec. 4) The bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to use Native American labor and purchase Native American industry products, unless Interior or HHS determines it would be impracticable and unreasonable to do so. Among other requirements, HHS and Interior must conduct outreach to Indian industrial entities in the implementation of enterprise development.

(Sec. 5) Additionally, the bill authorizes the Administration for Native Americans (ANA) to provide financial assistance to Native American community development financial institutions. ANA must give priority for financial assistance to applicants whose programs seek to develop (1) tribal codes and court systems relating to economic development, (2) tribal business structures, (3) community development financial institutions, or (4) tribal master plans for community and economic development and infrastructure.

summary.headline: A 2020 law that asks several federal agencies to support economic development in Native American communities, mainly through an Commerce Department office, a government study, and priority grants.
summary.what_it_does: The law gives the Office of Native American Business Development at the Department of Commerce duties to advise the department on U.S.-tribal relations and to serve as a point of contact for tribes, tribal organizations, and tribal members on economic development and doing business on Indian lands. It requires Commerce, Interior, and Treasury to coordinate efforts to support economic development in Native American communities. It also removes the matching-funds requirement for certain Community Development Financial Institutions Fund assistance that benefits Native American institutions, and it directs the Government Accountability Office to study existing Native American business programs, loan, bond, and tax incentive assistance, and alternative incentives for tribal governments to invest in community development funds or banks. Separately, it asks HHS to use Native American labor and buy Native American products unless Interior or HHS finds that doing so is impracticable and unreasonable, and it lets the Administration for Native Americans give financial help to Native American community development financial institutions, with priority for certain tribal economic development projects.

who_it_affects.group: Federally recognized tribes and tribal organizations
who_it_affects.how: They can contact the Office of Native American Business Development for help with economic development and doing business on Indian lands.

who_it_affects.group: Members of tribes starting or running businesses
who_it_affects.how: They can seek guidance from the Commerce Department office on economic development and doing business on Indian lands.

who_it_affects.group: Native American community development financial institutions
who_it_affects.how: They may get no-match assistance from the CDFI Fund and may receive financial help from the Administration for Native Americans, with priority for certain applicants.

who_it_affects.group: Tribal applicants seeking ANA funding for tribal codes, courts, business structures, or master plans
who_it_affects.how: Their applications for projects in these areas get priority for ANA financial assistance.

who_it_affects.group: Native American workers and Native American-made product suppliers
who_it_affects.how: HHS must use Native American labor and buy Native American products unless Interior or HHS finds this impracticable and unreasonable.
